Decide whether a string of digits and spaces passes the Luhn checksum.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/luhn) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: luhn.nomi
//# Validates numbers with the Luhn checksum.

/// Reports whether `number` passes the Luhn checksum. Spaces are ignored;
/// any other non-digit, or fewer than two digits, makes it invalid.
pub fn is_valid(number: String) -> Bool {
    digits =
        number
        |> String.replace(" ", "")
        |> Iter.map(String.to_int)
        |> Maybe.collect()

    case digits {
        Some(digits) when Iter.count(digits) > 1 -> checksum(digits) % 10 == 0
        _ -> False
    }
}

fn checksum(digits: List<Int>) -> Int {
    digits
    |> Iter.reverse()
    |> Iter.with_index()
    |> Iter.map(fn #(i, d) -> if i % 2 == 1 { double(d) } else { d })
    |> Iter.sum()
}

fn double(digit: Int) -> Int {
    doubled = digit * 2
    if doubled > 9 { doubled - 9 } else { doubled }
}

// FILE: luhn_test.nomi
import luhn

test "validates numbers with the Luhn checksum" {
    cases = [
        #("single digit strings can not be valid", "1", False),
        #("a single zero is invalid", "0", False),
        #("a simple valid SIN that remains valid if reversed", "059", True),
        #("a simple valid SIN that becomes invalid if reversed", "59", True),
        #("a valid Canadian SIN", "055 444 285", True),
        #("invalid Canadian SIN", "055 444 286", False),
        #("invalid credit card", "8273 1232 7352 0569", False),
        #("invalid long number with an even remainder", "1 2345 6789 1234 5678 9012", False),
        #(
            "invalid long number with a remainder divisible by 5",
            "1 2345 6789 1234 5678 9013",
            False,
        ),
        #("valid number with an even number of digits", "095 245 88", True),
        #("valid number with an odd number of spaces", "234 567 891 234", True),
        #("valid strings with a non-digit added at the end become invalid", "059a", False),
        #("valid strings with punctuation included become invalid", "055-444-285", False),
        #("valid strings with symbols included become invalid", "055# 444$ 285", False),
        #("single zero with space is invalid", " 0", False),
        #("more than a single zero is valid", "0000 0", True),
        #("input digit 9 is correctly converted to output digit 9", "091", True),
        #("very long input is valid", "9999999999 9999999999 9999999999 9999999999", True),
        #("valid luhn with an odd number of digits and non zero first digit", "109", True),
        #("using ascii value for non-doubled non-digit isn't allowed", "055b 444 285", False),
        #("using ascii value for doubled non-digit isn't allowed", ":9", False),
        #(
            "non-numeric, non-space char in the middle with a sum that's divisible by 10 isn't allowed",
            "59%59",
            False,
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, number, expected), description {
        assert luhn.is_valid(number) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Each grapheme goes through `String.to_int`, and `Maybe.collect` turns "every one is a digit" into one `Maybe<List<Int>>`, so a stray character and the digit conversion are one step.
- The length rule is a `when` guard on the `Some` arm rather than a separate `if`.
- `checksum` reverses the digits and doubles odd indexes from `Iter.with_index`, rather than tracking a parity flag in a fold, then totals them with `Iter.sum`.
- All 22 cases are one `subtests` table whose first column is the canonical description, which names each row.
